headline: Karl-Anthony Towns (illness) is questionable for Saturday’s game against the Trail Blazers.
body: Towns is a new addition to the Knicks’ injury report, and that’s generally not a good sign. If he can’t play, the Knicks will have to rely on Andre Drummond and James Wiseman to fill the void.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: OG Anunoby (calf) is now doubtful for Saturday’s game against the Trail Blazers.
body: Initially questionable for Saturday’s game, Anunoby is trending toward not playing. If he can’t play, Landry Shamet will likely enter the starting lineup, with Josh Hart sliding down to power forward.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Jabari Smith Jr. finished with 21 points (7-of-8 FGs), four rebounds, three assists and three three-pointers against the Nuggets on Friday.
body: Following a hot start to the season, Smith has cooled down a bit in the month of November. This was his first time scoring at least 20 points in a game since Oct. 31, and he only did it because he was insanely efficient. Hopefully, his volume will start to tick back up so he can get back to being elite for fantasy managers, as he was in October. He’ll look to carry this production into their next matchup with the Clippers on Monday.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Fred VanVleet lit up the Nuggets with 25 points (10-of-21 FGs), one rebound, nine assists, one steal and three three-pointers on Friday.
body: Despite missing all of last season, VanVleet has still been solid in fantasy basketball so far this year. He was able to set a new season high for scoring in this game, making this the first time he scored at least 25 points in a game since March of 2025. VanVleet’s presence in the lineup has been huge for Houston this year, and he proved in this game that he’s still capable of big scoring nights, even if they aren’t going to come consistently.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Luka Dončić put up 25 points (9-of-18 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), four rebounds, eight assists, two steals, two 3-pointers, and six turnovers in the 106-104 win over the Kings.
body: Luka continues to dominate the game and the Kings couldn’t do much to stop him. In the clutch, Keegan Murray did get a steal on him which could’ve cost the Lakers the game. You would wish the turnover numbers go down, but with the load that he’s had to do on offense, it’s hard to complain too much. He’s dominating everyone else from a statistical basis that is helping you in other areas.
author: Brian Taylor

headline: Alperen Şengün led the Rockets with 28 points (9-of-16 FGs, 9-of-13 FTs), 11 rebounds, 10 assists, one steal, one block and one three-pointer in a 133-124 loss to the Nuggets on Friday.
body: Şengün recorded his second triple-double of the season, but it wasn’t enough for Houston to secure the win. It has been a fantastic season for Şengün so far, as he is currently averaging career highs in points, assists, three-pointers and free throw percentage. He has been on the cusp of this type of production over the last few seasons, and it seems like he’s finally reaching it. The Rockets have started the season well, and Şengün has been right at the center of it.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Christian Braun lit up the Rockets with 19 points (7-of-10 FGs), five rebounds, three assists, four steals, one block and three three-pointers in a 133-124 win on Friday.
body: Last year was a down one for Braun, but he has bounced back to start this season. The offense is starting to pick up, but it’s his defensive impact that has been the biggest difference. He has at least one steal in every game this season and has had two or more in 10 of his 14 games, which has led to his career-high 2.3 steals per game. That’s carrying his category league value right now, which means he’s mostly been a one-trick pony, though he has been decent in a few other categories.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Quentin Grimes got himself 13 points (2-of-7 FGs, 8-of-9 FTs), five rebounds, seven assists, and a three in the win over the Kings on Friday.
body: Grimes started off slowly but got going later in the game and helped the Lakers hold on. He’s still worth holding, but coach JJ Reddick did say that he’s hoping to have Austin Reaves back on Monday against the Jazz, or on Friday against the San Antonio Spurs. So sell high if you can, or ride it out and drop when Reaves comes back.
author: Brian Taylor

headline: Cameron Johnson finished with 19 points (7-of-13 FGs), three rebounds, six assists, two steals and two three-pointers against the Rockets on Friday.
body: It has been another rough season in Denver for Johnson, but this was one of his best performances of the season, which included a new season high for assists. Johnson had a strong final season in Brooklyn, but he hasn’t been able to achieve that level of production during his two seasons as a Nugget. However, if he is able to provide lines like this, especially on a quieter night from Jamal Murray, Denver and fantasy managers will both be happy.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Walker Kessler put up 15 points (7-of-11 FGs, 0-of-2 FTs), seven rebounds, two assists, a steal, and three blocks, and a three in the win over the Kings.
body: Kessler had a very good game despite being in foul trouble. He had his way with Sabonis being in the paint and put up some good numbers. The two free throws he missed where in the clutch to ice the game. He hit a three in this game which was the first of the season. However, it’s a good performance all things considered.
author: Brian Taylor

headline: DeMar DeRozan provided a boost off the bench with 15 points (4-of-11 FGs), two rebounds, two assists and one steal against the Rockets on Friday.
body: DeRozan started this season scoring in double figures in each of Denver’s first three games. In the 10 games since, he has only scored in double figures three more times. The positive news is that he’s reached that mark in back-to-back games. DeRozan isn’t going to provide value anywhere near what he has throughout his career, but if he can continue to be a reliable bench scorer for Denver, he’ll be a valuable piece for this team when the playoffs arrive.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Domantas Sabonis got himself 19 points (8-of-13 FGs, 2-of-3 FTs), 16 rebounds, an assist and a three in the loss to the Lakers on Friday.
body: Sabonis continues to chug along and be efficient from the field. He did a good job on the offensive end and helping keep the Kings in the game, but he didn’t do a good job preventing Walker Kessler from having a good game. He at least got more shot attempts in this game after it’s been lackluster for the past few games.
author: Brian Taylor

headline: Alperen Şengün (eye) will be available against the Nuggets on Friday.
body: Şengün sustained the injury against the Pacers in the second quarter and didn’t return. He should hopefully go back to producing at the level he was prior to the injury. He’s averaging 21.6 points, 9.2 rebounds, and 6.8 assists on the season.
author: Brian Taylor

headline: Steven Adams (quad) is available to play against the Nuggets on Friday.
body: Adams was initially listed as questionable for this game, but he will be good to go. With Alperen Şengün available, Adams will fill out the backup center minutes.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Lakers head coach JJ Redick said the “hope” is that Austin Reaves (heel) will return in one of the Lakers’ next two games.
body: Following their matchup with the Kings on Friday, the Lakers will play the Jazz at home on Monday and the Spurs in San Antonio on Friday. It’s good to have some clarity on Reaves’ injury, but it also means Quentin Grimes’ time as a starter is likely coming to an end. If Reaves waits until Friday to play, Grimes should be streamed on Monday.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Derrick White (shoulder) is questionable for Saturday’s game against the Kings.
body: If White were to miss time, look for Payton Pritchard to be the main beneficiary of the absence. After that, it’s likely to be a lot of the Celtics role players getting marginal bumps.
author: Brian Taylor

headline: Jayson Tatum (rest) is questionable to play against the Kings on Saturday.
body: Boston may be looking to give Tatum a night off against Sacramento before they play the Warriors on Saturday. If that’s the case, Sam Hauser will likely get the starting nod in place of Tatum.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: The Thunder will start Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Ajay Mitchell, Jared McCain, Aday Mara, and Isaiah Hartenstein against the Pelicans on Friday.
body: It was previously reported that Micah Peavy would be starting in place Aday Mara, but Mara will get the nod. Mara is a streamer and Peavy isn’t anything more than a deeper league guy.
author: Brian Taylor

headline: The Raptors will start Immanuel Quickley, Ja’Kobe Walter, Scottie Barnes, Allen Graves, and Jakob Poeltl on Friday against the Pistons.
body: Collin Murray-Boyles will not play tonight and is replaced by rookie Allen Graves. Given Graves’s fantasy profile, if you want to stream him in, you might get a good performance.
author: Brian Taylor

headline: Ron Holland (knee) has been ruled out against the Raptors on Friday.
body: For some reason, Detroit upgraded Holland to doubtful ahead of this game, and he has now officially been ruled out. This will be a third straight absence for him, which should allow Isaiah Joe and Chaz Lanier to continue taking on a few extra minutes.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: The Cavaliers will start James Harden, Donovan Mitchell, Tyrese Proctor, Peyton Watson, and Jarrett Allen on Friday against the Pacers.
body: Peyton Watson returns to the starting lineup with Mario Hezonja heading back to the bench. For now, Watson is just a stream guy and Hezonja is only a deeper league type of player.
author: Brian Taylor Mario Hezonja

headline: Cade Cunningham (knee) is available to play against the Raptors on Friday.
body: As expected, Cunningham will return following a one-game absence. Javonte Green, who was excellent as a spot starter, will return to playing a role off the bench.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: The Nets will start Nolan Traoré, Danny Wolf, Michael Porter Jr., Julius Randle, and Day’Ron Sharpe on Friday against Bulls.
body: The Nets will replace Egor in the starting lineup and replace him with Danny Wolf. This will be something to monitor going forward, but for now, Wolf could be used as a streamer and we’ll see how coach Jordi Fernandez distributes the minutes.
author: Brian Taylor Egor Dëmin

headline: Noa Essengue (wrist) will be available to play Friday against the Wizards.
body: Noa was listed as probable before this game, so it’s good to see that he’s giving it a go. Hopefully it doesn’t flare up and have him miss some time. Noa is just a deeper league guy, even with the Caleb Wilson injury.
author: Brian Taylor

headline: T.J. McConnell (hamstring) is available to play against the Cavaliers on Friday.
body: McConnell was initially listed as probable for this game, so his availability doesn’t come as a surprise. He continues to pop up on the injury report, but he hasn’t missed a game since he made his season debut two weeks ago. He may lose a few minutes with Andrew Nembhard back.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Peyton Watson (back) will be available to play against the Pacers on Friday.
body: He missed the past couple games with a back injury. With him coming back, it is possible that he returns to the starting lineup and causes Sam Merrill to come back to the bench. As of right now, he’s only a stream option for most redraft leagues.
author: Brian Taylor

headline: Trey Murphy (knee) will play but with a minutes limit against the Thunder on Friday.
body: Murphy returns from a six game absence from a knee injury. With him returning, Saddiq Bey will likely head back to the bench and still be an option if you need points and three’s.
author: Brian Taylor

headline: Alex Caruso (hip) will not play against the Pelicans on Friday.
body: He played nine minutes against the Hawks before leaving with a hip injury and didn’t return. Look for Bennett Stirtz and Nique Clifford to take more minutes in this game, but both of them are deeper league options and not streamers in most redraft leagues.
author: Brian Taylor

headline: Jalen Smith (illness) has been ruled out against the Wizards on Friday.
body: Smith will be sidelined for this game after popping up on the injury report with a gastrointestinal illness earlier in the day. Nic Claxton will likely get the start at center, with Zach Collins filling out the backup minutes down low.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: Jerami Grant (left calf strain) will not play on Saturday against the Timberwolves.
body: He left Thursday’s game after five minutes and didn’t return. Olivier Maxence-Prosper and Taylor Hendricks were the beneficiaries of that injury. Hendricks could be used as a streamer in twelve team leagues and Maxence-Prosper is a deeper league guy.
author: Brian Taylor

headline: Javon Small (personal) has been ruled out against the Timberwolves on Saturday.
body: Small has been an important reserve for Memphis this season, especially as of late. With Ty Jerome expected to return from a four-game absence, Small’s minutes will go to Cam Spencer, who filled in nicely as a starter with Jerome out.
author: Noah Rubin

headline: ESPN’s Shams Charania reports Brandon Ingram (Achilles) is expected to make his season debut against the Rockets on Monday.
body: Ingram has been traveling with the team recently with signs pointing towards an imminent debut. Now Charania has reported that will come Monday against the Rockets. The 29-year-old forward’s return from a partially torn Achilles also coincides with a four-game week for the Clippers.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Ron Holland (knee) is doubtful for Friday’s game against the Raptors.
body: Holland is unlikely to suit up Friday as he’s listed as doubtful with a left knee contusion. The 21-year-old forward was present at shootaround Friday, which is a good sign that the injury isn’t overly serious. Holland’s likely absence Friday won’t impact fantasy basketball.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Jalen Smith (illness) is questionable for Friday’s game against the Wizards.
body: Smith popped up on the injury report Friday as questionable with an illness. He’s potentially on the wrong side of questionable given that he only has a few hours to recover before the game. If the 26-year-old forward is ruled out, Nic Claxton could move into the starting lineup.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Stephon Castle had 21 points (7-of-12 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), six rebounds, 12 assists, four steals and two three-pointers against the Clippers on Thursday.
body: Castle bounced back nicely after scoring only 10 points against the Pistons on Tuesday. He has now recorded at least 20 points in three of his last four games. The 22-year-old guard has also posted at least six assists in four consecutive games and at least four steals in two of his last three games. The Spurs have one game remaining this week, against the Pelicans at home Saturday.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Julian Champagnie had 20 points (8-of-14 FGs, 0-of-2 FTs), four rebounds, one assist and four three-pointers against the Clippers on Thursday.
body: Champagnie moved into the starting lineup Thursday and will likely remain there with Dylan Harper (hip) set to be sidelined for weeks. The 25-year-old forward scored 20 points and made four three-pointers in 29 minutes. He’ll be especially useful to fantasy managers in need of three-point shooting while Harper is out.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Victor Wembanyama had 32 points (13-of-26 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), 11 rebounds, three assists, one block, one steal and two three-pointers in the Spurs’ 124-112 victory over the Clippers on Thursday.
body: Wembanyama had another excellent game, though he continues to struggle from behind the three-point line. The 22-year-old center is just 3-of-15 from behind the arc over his last two games. Still one of the best players in all of fantasy basketball, Wembanyama’s next chance to break out of his shooting slump will come Saturday against the Pelicans at home.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Charles Bassey had 16 points (6-of-7 FGs, 4-of-5 FTs), 13 rebounds, one assist, one steal and two blocks against the Grizzlies on Thursday.
body: Bassey was a bright spot for the Warriors on Thursday. The 26-year-old forward led the team with 16 points and had a double-double with 13 rebounds. Bassey was still able to put up a solid fantasy stat line in just 24 minutes. He’s worthy of streaming consideration when he’s in the starting lineup.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Cedric Coward had 19 points (7-of-14 FGs), four rebounds, four assists, one steal, one block and five three-pointers against the Warriors on Thursday.
body: Coward is a steady player who contributes fantasy production across the board. The 23-year-old guard once again posted a complete stat line against the Warriors Thursday. Coward should remain in fantasy lineups heading into Saturday’s game against the Timberwolves on the road.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Jaylen Wells had 22 points (8-of-10 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), seven rebounds and four three-pointers in the Grizzlies’ 126-98 victory over the Warriors on Thursday.
body: Wells had a nice game Thursday against the Warriors with 22 points and seven rebounds. The 23-year-old forward got hot from downtown, sinking four three-pointers. Unfortunately, Wells doesn’t offer much outside of points and threes and is tough to roster in most fantasy basketball formats.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Nate Ament had 18 points (6-of-11 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), nine rebounds and two three-pointers against the Trail Blazers on Thursday.
body: Ament moved into the starting lineup Thursday and the 19-year-old forward had a great game. Ament played 35 minutes and had 18 points and nine rebounds. He proved he’s worth streaming consideration when given the opportunity to start.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Jrue Holiday had 22 points (8-of-14 FGs, 4-of-5 FTs), two rebounds, seven assists, four steals and two three-pointers against the Bucks on Thursday.
body: Holiday has now recorded at least 21 points, at least six assists and at least three combined steals and blocks in back-to-back games. He stepped up with 22 points on 14 attempts with Deni Avdija (foot) out Thursday. Holiday will continue to see a boost in fantasy value if Avdija remains out.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Scoot Henderson had 27 points (8-of-12 FGs, 6-of-7 FTs), seven rebounds, three assists, one block, one steal and five three-pointers against the Bucks on Thursday.
body: Henderson stepped up with Deni Avdija (foot) out of the lineup Thursday. The 22-year-old guard came out of nowhere to drop 27 points off the bench, which helped lead to a 124-114 victory over the Bucks. Henderson has to be more consistent to merit fantasy consideration, but, for one night, he certainly had an outstanding game.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Damian Lillard had 33 points (10-of-18 FGs, 8-of-9 FTs), six rebounds and five three-pointers in the Trail Blazers’ 124-114 victory over the Bucks on Thursday.
body: In Lillard’s first game against the Bucks in Milwaukee since he was waived by the organization two summers ago, the 36-year-old guard predictably lit them up. Lillard torched the Bucks’ defense for 33 points on 18 attempts, connecting on five three-pointers in the process. The Trail Blazers have one game remaining this week against the Knicks on the road Saturday.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Jonathan Kuminga had 23 points (7-of-13 FGs, 7-of-7 FTs), three rebounds, three assists, three blocks and two three-pointers against the Knicks on Thursday.
body: Kuminga returned to the floor after a one-game absence due to a shoulder injury. The 24-year-old forward had 23 points, which led the Timberwolves in the loss to the Knicks Thursday. Kuminga will look to build on this performance as his production has been inconsistent at best despite increased opportunities with Anthony Edwards (knee) sidelined. His next opportunity will come against the Grizzlies at home on Saturday.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Jalen Brunson had 21 points (8-of-20 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), two rebounds, seven assists, two steals and four three-pointers against the Timberwolves on Thursday.
body: Brunson has now posted four three-pointers and at least seven assists in three of his last four games. The 30-year-old guard wasn’t very efficient with 21 points on 20 attempts, but he also recorded seven assists and only one turnover. Brunson and the Knicks begin a home back-to-back against the Trail Blazers and Pacers on Saturday.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Karl-Anthony Towns had 22 points (9-of-20 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), 12 rebounds, four assists, three blocks and two three-pointers in the Knicks’ 102-99 victory over the Timberwolves on Thursday.
body: Towns has now recorded at least 21 points in six of his last seven games. The 31-year-old center also leads the league in rebounds per game with 13.9. In the midst of contract turmoil, Towns is having one of his best seasons, which is great news for fantasy managers.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Jerami Grant (calf) won’t return to Thursday’s game against the Warriors.
body: After making a three-pointer early in the second quarter, Grant limped back to the locker room before being ruled out with a left calf injury. He finished with three points in five minutes.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: De’Andre Hunter (hip) is questionable for Friday’s game against the Lakers.
body: Hunter returned to the starting lineup Wednesday after a one-game absence due to a hip injury. He’s on the injury report for Friday as questionable with the same hip injury. Dylan Cardwell could move into the starting lineup if Hunter is out again.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Austin Reaves (heel) is out for Friday’s game against the Kings.
body: No surprise here as there’s still no timetable for Reaves to return from a heel injury. Friday will be his fourth missed game in a row. Quentin Grimes should continue to start in his absence.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: The Bucks will start Brayden Burries, Tyler Herro, Nate Amnet, Larry Nance and Kel’el Ware against the Trail Blazers on Thursday.
body: The Bucks have a fresh frontline with Amnet, Nance and Ware all getting the starting nod Thursday. Ware is the most interesting option for fantasy as he should see a significant increase in usage with Myles Turner (shoulder) sidelined.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: The Clippers will start Darius Garland, Max Strus, Derrick Jones Jr., Rui Hachimura and Brook Lopez against the Spurs on Thursday.
body: Los Angeles is changing things up tonight with Strus starting in place of Kris Dunn, who will come off the bench. Neither have been viable in fantasy basketball leagues this season, but we’ll see how this goes.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: The Spurs will start De’Aaron Fox, Stephon Castle, Devin Vassell, Julian Champagnie and Victor Wembanyama against the Clippers on Thursday.
body: No surprise here as with Dylan Harper (hip) sidelined for weeks, the Spurs have moved Champagnie into the starting lineup. The 25-year-old forward can be useful to fantasy managers, especially those in need of three-point shooting.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Warriors will start De’Anthony Melton, Brandin Podziemski, Gui Santos, Yaxel Lendeborg and Charles Bassey against the Grizzlies on Thursday.
body: Even with LJ Cryer (back) available, Melton will start for the Warriors. The only other change in the starting lineup for Golden State is Santos subbing in for Draymond Green.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: The Grizzlies will start Cam Spencer, Cedric Coward, Jaylen Wells, Cam Boozer and Taylor Hendricks against the Warriors on Thursday.
body: With Zach Edey (ankle) out of the lineup, Hendricks will start in his absence. Isaiah Stewart (illness) is also available and figures to play a significant role off the bench.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Jonathan Kuminga (shoulder) is available for Thursday’s game against the Knicks.
body: Kuminga is set to return after missing Tuesday’s game against the Trail Blazers with a right shoulder contusion. Cody Williams will move back to the bench with Kuminga in the starting lineup Thursday.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Toumani Camara (soreness) is available for Thursday’s game against the Bucks.
body: Camara is available after being listed as questionable with soreness. The 26-year-old forward is in the middle of an iron man streak with Thursday marking his 101st consecutive regular season game.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Deni Avdija (foot) is out for Thursday’s game against the Bucks.
body: Avdija is set to miss his second game in a row with a foot injury. Jayson Kent figures to start again while Jrue Holiday stands to gain the most fantasy value in Avdija’s absence.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Peyton Watson (back) is questionable for Friday’s game against the Pacers.
body: Watson has missed two of the last three games with a lower back issue. His questionable status at least gives him a chance of suiting up Friday against the Pacers. If Watson is out, Sam Merrill could take on a larger role.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Jaylon Tyson (ankle) is out for Friday’s game against the Pacers.
body: Tyson will miss a third straight game as he manages a right ankle injury that sidelined him for six games in late October/early November. If Peyton Watson (back), who’s questionable for Friday, remains out, Mario Hezonja could remain in the starting lineup.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Scottie Barnes (groin) is not on the injury report for Friday’s game against the Pistons.
body: Barnes is back after sitting out Wednesday’s loss to the Wizards. With Collin Murray-Boyles in the league’s concussion protocol, Jakob Poeltl could remain in the starting lineup despite Barnes’ return.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Eubka Okorie (oblique) is out for Friday’s game against the Raptors.
body: Okorie, who last appeared in a game on November 9 against the Raptors, has played 21 minutes over five appearances for the Pistons this season. His absence won’t affect fantasy basketball.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Taurean Prince (knee) is out for Friday’s game against the Raptors.
body: Prince has appeared in three games for the Pistons this season, totaling 21 minutes. His absence won’t affect fantasy basketball.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Ron Holland (knee) is out for Friday’s game against the Raptors.
body: After missing both games of the Pistons’ back-to-back on Tuesday and Wednesday, Holland will miss a third straight game on Friday. Isaiah Joe’s return from a hip injury has given the Pistons additional wing depth, and Chaz Lanier has played rotation minutes the last two games.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Cade Cunningham (knee) is probable for Friday’s game against the Raptors.
body: Cunningham did not play in Wednesday’s win over the Pelicans, sitting out due to a sore right knee. His likely return on Friday would push Javonte Green, who scored 18 points on Wednesday, to the bench.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Grant Nelson (ankle) is out for Friday’s game against the Magic.
body: Nelson, who appeared in four games last season, has yet to play for the Nets this season. His absence won’t affect fantasy basketball.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: RJ Barrett has been diagnosed with a mild right hamstring strain and will be re-evaluated in two weeks.
body: Barrett was held out of Wednesday’s loss to the Wizards after playing 39 minutes in Tuesday’s loss to the Knicks. The injury was initially diagnosed as right hamstring tightness, but the Raptors now say it’s a strain. With Barrett sidelined, the Raptors will have to rely more on Scottie Barnes and Immanuel Quickley offensively, and Jamison Battle could move into the starting lineup.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Collin Murray-Boyles was placed in concussion protocol.
body: Murray-Boyles was placed in concussion protocol as a precaution, according to the Raptors. The 21-year-old forward’s timeline to return is unknown. Trayce Jackson-Davis enters the Raptors rotation in Murray-Boyles’ absence, but isn’t a priority in fantasy leagues.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Dylan Harper (hip) has been diagnosed with a left hip external rotator strain and is expected to miss 2-3 weeks.
body: Harper suffered the injury in the final minute of Tuesday’s loss to the Pistons and required assistance to return to the locker room. His absence is a big deal for the Spurs, as the second-year guard has been playing well, but things could have been worse. Julian Champagnie, who can provide solid fantasy value, especially for managers needing three-pointers, should move into the starting lineup.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Anthony Edwards (knee) said Thursday that he has “no clue” when asked about a potential return timeline.
body: Edwards underwent an arthroscopic procedure on his right knee in October, and it was reported that he could be out for over two months. When asked about his recovery progress, Edwards said that he was unsure when he’d be able to play again. He hoped to avoid needing surgery, but that became unavoidable once the knee flared up after the regular season began. “It was good in [training] camp, like I said,” Edwards said. “I think after the Miami game it started to flare up, and then it went down a little bit after the Orlando game, so we thought we were going to be alright, but then after the back-to-back it was really bad, like painful to fly, so I’m like, ‘I gotta get it.” Ayo Dosunmu has been the starter with Edwards out and should be rostered in most fantasy leagues until that changes.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Kyle Kuzma (shoulder) is out for Thursday’s game against the Trail Blazers.
body: Kuzma will miss Thursday’s game with a right shoulder contusion after playing 30 minutes in Wednesday’s loss to the Heat. Jaime Jaquez Jr. is not guaranteed to start, but his role should expand with Kuzma sidelined.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Myles Turner (shoulder) is out for Thursday’s game against the Trail Blazers.
body: Turner, who played 21 minutes in Wednesday’s loss to the Heat, is out with a left shoulder contusion. Kel’el Ware and Jericho Sims should see their minutes increase. While Ware offers a higher upside, his inconsistency has been an issue.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Ryan Rollins (illness) is not on the injury report for Thursday’s game against the Trail Blazers.
body: Rollins is available after sitting out Wednesday’s loss to the Heat. His return may lead to fewer minutes for Kasparas Jakučionis.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Isaiah Stewart (illness) is questionable for Thursday’s game against the Warriors.
body: Stewart has missed the Grizzlies’ last two games due to an illness. With Zach Edey (ankle) out, Beef Stew could start on Thursday if available. If he sits, Quinten Post and Taylor Hendricks will handle most of the center responsibilities.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Ty Jerome (hip) is out for Thursday’s game against the Warriors.
body: Jerome will miss a fourth straight game with a right hip impingement. Cam Spencer has played well as his replacement in the starting lineup and should probably be rostered in some 12-team leagues even after Jerome returns.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Al Horford (rest) is not on the injury report for Thursday’s game against the Grizzlies.
body: Horford is available after sitting out Wednesday’s loss to the Mavericks. With Draymond Green (elbow) out, Horford could move into the starting lineup out of necessity.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Marcus Smart (suspension) finished Wednesday’s win over the Pacers with four points (1-of-4 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), two rebounds, four assists, one steal, one block and one three-pointer.
body: After serving a three-game suspension for throwing a punch at Warriors center Charles Bassey, Smart returned to the Rockets’ rotation on Wednesday. He took on his usual bench role, which offers little fantasy value when Fred VanVleet and Reed Sheppard are available. Fantasy managers can leave Smart on the waiver wire, as he’s scored in double figures twice in 10 games this season.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Jaxson Hayes (knee) finished Wednesday’s win over the Lakers with six points (2-of-5 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), seven rebounds, two assists, two steals and two blocks.
body: Available after a two-game absence, Hayes came off the bench on Wednesday night. However, he still played more than starter Mo Bamba, who logged 22 minutes and finished with six points, 16 rebounds, one steal and two blocks. With that minutes split in Hayes’ first game back, it may not take him long to move into the starting lineup.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Walker Kessler had a stat line of 10 points (3-of-7 FGs, 4-of-10 FTs), 11 rebounds, and an assist against his former team, the Jazz on Wednesday.
body: Walker Kessler had a good performance except for the free throw percentage where he went 4-of-10. There might be a slight buy low opportunity here for Walker if someone is mad about the FT% and the lack of scoring that he’s had over the past few games. He should bounce back, but he’s not the player that people saw in the first two games of the season where he looked amazing.
author: Brian Taylor

headline: Quentin Grimes got 20 points (8-of-20 FGs, 7-of-7 FTs), seven rebounds, four assists, and four 3-pointers in loss on Wednesday to Jazz.
body: Grimes continued his run after an insane game against the Hornets on Tuesday. He’s been the big beneficiary of the Reaves injury at this point. He’s wroth having until Reaves comes back, but once he does, he’s a streamer for points and 3’s only. The usage won’t be the same as it was during this run. This is a sell high if you have him on your roster currently.
author: Brian Taylor

headline: Luka Dončić scored 29 points (10-of-28 FGs, 7-of-7 FTs), got five rebounds, seven assists, two steals, two 3-pointers, and 9 turnovers in 109-97 loss to Jazz.
body: The run that Luka is on this season is incredible. You can pencil him in for a great game every night and there’s nothing the opponent can do about it. It wasn’t even the best night and he still produced. You wish the turnovers are lower, but he’s having to do everything for this team, especially with Austin Reaves out of the lineup.
author: Brian Taylor

headline: Ace Bailey got himself 19 points (7-of-19 FGs, 3-of-3 FTs), eight rebounds, three assists, a steal, and two 3-pointers on Wednesday.
body: Ace has been more inconsistent as of late with his shooting, but the Jazz needed offense with Darryn being in foul trouble, and Ace at least put up shots and impacted the game in other ways defensively. There might be a bit of a buy low still with the efficiency, especially with the 3PT shooting being as low as it is, but he’s been great this year for the Jazz.
author: Brian Taylor

headline: Svi Mykhailiuk put up 15 points (4-of-10 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), three rebounds, five assists, two steals and four 3-pointers in win on Wednesday.
body: It’s been a terrible start to the season for Svi. He wasn’t going to continue to shoot as poorly as he has, so it’s nice to see a decent bounce back game from him. He’s only a player for deeper leagues as a streamer, but it’s good to commend him for his performance tonight since he played 34 minutes with Darryn Peterson getting into foul trouble.
author: Brian Taylor

headline: Keyonte Geroge scores 30 points (9-of-17 FGs, 7-of-9 FTs), a rebound, ten assists, a steal, and five 3-pointers in the 109-97 win over the Lakers.
body: George was carrying the offense for the Jazz and keeping them in the first half of this game. Darryn Peterson was having foul trouble, so it was on him to keep the Jazz in the game. He helped lead them to get the win in this one. It’s been great back-to-back games for Keyonte and there might be a sell high window here.
author: Brian Taylor

headline: Jayson Tatum had 24 points (10-of-23 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), eight rebounds, three assists, one steal and three three-pointers against the Nuggets on Wednesday.
body: Tatum led the Celtics with 24 points Wednesday, but a late technical foul proved costly in the loss to the Nuggets. The 28-year-old forward was assessed a technical foul in the final seconds of the game for throwing the ball in the direction of an official. This allowed Jamal Murray to make the technical free throw and ice the game for the Nuggets by extending the Denver lead to four. The Celtics begin a back-to-back against the Kings and Warriors on the road Saturday.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Jamal Murray had 21 points (7-of-15 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), seven rebounds, two assists, four steals, two blocks and two three-pointers against the Celtics on Wednesday.
body: Murray was excellent and finished with a complete stat line against the Celtics Wednesday. The 29-year-old guard hit a clutch jumper to put the Nuggets up by three with less than 10 seconds left in regulation. Following a technical foul on Jayson Tatum, Murray then hit a free throw to ice the game. Denver improved to 8-5 on the season while the Celtics fell to 11-4.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Domantas Sabonis accounted for eight points (4-of-7 FGs), 13 rebounds, eight assists and one steal in Wednesday’s loss to the Suns.
body: Sabonis’ rebounding and assist numbers will certainly help fantasy managers. However, he attempted seven shots against the Suns, dropping his season average to 8.6 attempts per game. He’s struggled more than fellow veteran Zach LaVine to adjust to rookie guard Darius Acuff Jr. However, Domas is still providing top-50 fantasy value because of what he’s done outside of scoring.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Zach LaVine tallied 18 points (8-of-12 FGs), five rebounds, two assists, one steal and two three-pointers in Wednesday’s loss to the Suns.
body: LaVine returned to the Kings’ lineup on Wednesday after an illness kept him out of Sunday’s loss to the Thunder. While he shot the ball well, the veteran guard’s presence was enough to keep the Kings from finishing their home stand with a seventh straight loss. LaVine has been close to a top-50 player so far, outperforming his ADP.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Charles Bassey put up 10 points (5-of-8 FGs, 0-of-2 FTs), eight rebounds, a steal, a block, and four turnovers in loss.
body: Bassey has been a great find for the Warriors this season. They’ve needed his rebounding and presence in the paint considering that they haven’t had Kristaps all season, and Horford is older. In redraft leagues, he’s primarily a streamer and not much more than that.
author: Brian Taylor

headline: Yaxel Lendeborg gets 13 points (6-of-18 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), five rebounds, five assists, and two steals in the 116-94 loss to the Mavericks.
body: For the numbers that Yaxel has been putting up since Steph has gone out, it wasn’t a great game. The Warriors as a team have really been missing Steph and his presence on the court. He’s been getting shots up which is great to see, but it hasn’t resulted in wins. In a redraft league, he’s been a great steal from where you got him.
author: Brian Taylor

headline: Will Richards had himself a night with 20 points (9-of-13 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), three assists, four steals, and a three in the loss to the Mavericks.
body: Will was the only players on the Warriors that could get his offense consistently in this game. It’s honestly impressive considering he’s playing with his thumb wrapped up and he was hitting shots in this one. Getting the four steals is a nice bump, even getting one on his college teammate Walter Clayton. It’s a great performance, but it’s hard to project anything like this happening from him going forward.
author: Brian Taylor

headline: Daniss Jenkins had 17 points (7-of-16 FGs), four rebounds, nine assists and three three-pointers in the Pistons’ 122-109 victory over the Pelicans on Wednesday.
body: Jenkins has been excellent as he’s helped the Pistons to wins over the Spurs and Pelicans on back-to-back nights. The 25-year-old guard combined for 42 points, nine rebounds and 14 assists in the last two games. The Pistons resume NBA Cup play Friday against the Raptors at home.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Nikola Topić (hip) did not return for the second half of Wednesday’s loss to the Hawks.
body: - Raphielle Johnson

headline: Kyrie Irving had 17 points (7-of-15 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), six rebounds, five assists, three steals, and a three in the 116-94 win over the Mavericks.
body: Another very standard Kyrie game where did everything necessary to get you the win. You’d wish for more points, but getting the six rebounds is a nice bump from what Kyrie has been averaging on the season. The Mavs next play the Clippers on Saturday.
author: Brian Taylor

headline: Alex Caruso (hip) did not return for the second half of Wednesday’s loss to the Hawks.
body: - Raphielle Johnson

headline: P.J. Washington had 21 points (7-of-10 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), five rebounds, two assists, a steal, three blocks, and five 3-pointers in win on Wednesday against Warriors.
body: P.J. Washington had his random game where he explodes and hits most of his shots. Before this game, he was averaging less than a steal and a block, so naturally he got a steal and three blocks in this one. He’s nothing more than a streamer and if you want some points, threes, and rebounds.
author: Brian Taylor

headline: Isaiah Hartenstein finished Wednesday’s loss to the Hawks with six points (3-of-5 FGs), 17 rebounds, six assists and two blocks.
body: - Raphielle Johnson

headline: Cooper Flagg put up 33 points (11-of-15 FGs, 8-of-8 FTs), five rebounds, nine assists, three steals, three 3-pointers, and five turnovers in win.
body: The small buy low window has officially closed with this blowout performance against the Warriors. Now, it’s still the Warriors without Stephen Curry, so it’s not like the team has been an incredibly good team, but it’s good to see him get back on track. He will likely finish in the first-round range of most redraft leagues.
author: Brian Taylor

headline: Cavaliers waived Riley Minix and signed Zack Austin to a two-way contract.
body: Minix, who agreed to a two-way contract on November 7, appeared in four games for the Cavaliers before being waived. This transaction corresponds with Cleveland signing Zack Austin to a two-way contract.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: The Toronto Raptors will start Immanuel Quickley, Ja’Kobe Walter, Jamison Battle, Collin Murray-Boyles, and Jakob Poeltl on Wednesday against the Wizards.
body: RJ Barrett (hamstring) will not be available in Wednesday’s game, so Jamison Battle is getting the start. Battle is a streamer for 3’s but he doesn’t do much else in category leagues.
author: Brian Taylor Jamison Battle

headline: Tobi Lawal (groin) is out for Wednesday’s game against the Warriors.
body: Lawal’s absence won’t impact fantasy basketball or the Mavericks’ rotation, as Santi Aldama (ankle) is back after missing Sunday’s loss to the Celtics.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Walter Clayton Jr. (ankle) is available for Wednesday’s game against the Warriors.
body: Clayton is available after playing 23 minutes in Sunday’s loss to the Celtics. However, his playing time could decrease, as Kyrie Irving is back after not playing in Boston.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Max Christie (ankle) will play against the Warriors on Wednesday.
body: Christie will return from a two game absence from an ankle injury. He will likely take Marcus Sasser out of the rotation and possibly some minutes from Walter Clayton Jr. Christie is nothing more than a streamer for most redraft leagues.
author: Brian Taylor

headline: Santi Aldama (ankle) is available for Wednesday’s game against the Warriors.
body: Initially probable for Wednesday’s game, Aldama is officially available. His return likely means that Moussa Cissé won’t play unless the game gets out of hand. This does not affect fantasy basketball.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Jaylin Williams (back) will return to the court on Wednesday against the Hawks.
body: Williams has missed the past seven games with a back injury. With his return, we could see a reduction in minutes for Aday Mara, Kenrich Williams, Micah Peavy and Josh Dix depending on how the Thunder want to matchup against the Hawks.
author: Brian Taylor

headline: Al Horford (injury management) will not play against the Mavericks on Wednesday, but will play on Thursday against Grizzlies.
body: Horford has not been what you would’ve hoped this season but that is to be expected with his age. On a low volume day, you could consider a stream of Horford as Draymond Green will be out, but the minutes won’t be very high and he’ll likely only be useful in deeper leagues.
author: Brian Taylor

headline: Anfernee Simons, VJ Edgecombe, Kentavious Caldwell-Pope, LeBron James and Joel Embiid will start Wednesday’s game against the Magic.
body: The 76ers are down two starters, as Tyrese Maxey (foot) and Jaylen Brown (hamstring) are out. Simons and Caldwell-Pope have moved into the starting lineup, and both are worth streaming due to Philadelphia’s lack of depth.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Precious Achiuwa (ankle) is available for Wednesday’s game against the Suns.
body: Achiuwa missed two games with left ankle soreness, but is set to return Wednesday against the Suns. Keegan Murray will likely return to the bench with Achiuwa back in the lineup.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: De’Andre Hunter (hip) is available for Wednesday’s game against the Suns.
body: Hunter missed Sunday’s loss to the Thunder with a hip injury. Dylan Cardwell will likely head back to the bench with Hunter returning to the starting lineup Wednesday against the Suns.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Jaxson Hayes (knee) is questionable for Wednesday’s game against the Lakers.
body: Hayes has missed the last two games with a strained left knee, allowing Mo Bamba to start. His questionable status gives him a chance to return Wednesday, but if not Bamba will likely start again and could be worth streaming.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Walker Kessler (leg) is off the injury report ahead of Wednesday’s game against the Jazz.
body: Kessler missed Tuesday’s win over the Hornets with leg soreness. He’s set to return Wednesday against the Jazz, his former team. Kevon Looney will head back to the bench with Kessler back in the lineup.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Austin Reaves (heel) is out for Wednesday’s game against the Jazz.
body: Reaves will miss his third game in a row with a heel injury. Quentin Grimes should continue starting in Reaves’ absence and should be rostered in all formats.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Luka Dončić (ankle) is not listed on the injury report ahead of Wednesday’s game against the Jazz.
body: Dončić (ankle) had 36 points in Tuesday’s win over the Hornets. Off the injury report Wednesday, he will suit up again Wednesday against the Jazz on the second night of a back-to-back.
author: Nick Shlain

headline: Isaiah Joe (hip) has been upgraded to questionable for Wednesday’s matchup with the Pelicans.
body: Joe has a chance to return for the first time since October 25, and the Pistons could use him, as several key players are on the injury report for the second leg of Detroit’s back-to-back set.
author: Zak Hanshew

headline: Peyton Watson (back) has been downgraded to doubtful for Wednesday’s matchup with Memphis.
body: Watson played Monday, but he’s expected to sit out while dealing with a lower-back contusion. In his absence, Meleek Thomas and Mario Hezonja should see more playing time.
author: Zak Hanshew

headline: Jaylon Tyson (ankle) is out for Wednesday’s matchup with the Grizzlies.
body: Tyson was listed as doubtful on Tuesday, so his absence Wednesday isn’t surprising. Tyrese Proctor should continue to log additional minutes while Tyson is out, making him worth a look off the waiver wire.
author: Zak Hanshew

headline: Brandon Miller notched 28 points (10-of-19 FGs, 3-of-3 FTs), two rebounds, four assists, one block and five three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Lakers.
body: Fantasy managers have been waiting for Miller to snap out of his shooting slump for quite some time, and he may have done so on Tuesday. The Hornets wing shot over 50 percent from the field, and 28 points was the most he’s scored in a game since October 28 against the Pistons. Miller has been asked to create more looks for himself off the dribble, and it’s been a struggle. Miller is still shooting 35.9 percent from the field, so the buy-low window may not be closed just yet. Also, while he played 32 minutes, the Hornets shut Miller down at the end of regulation, leaving him to watch overtime from the bench.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Naz Reid (nose) accounted for 23 points (8-of-18 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), 11 rebounds, four assists, two steals, two blocks and four three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Lakers.
body: The line Reid recorded against the Lakers was in line with what many fantasy managers hoped to see from him consistently in Charlotte. Unfortunately, things haven’t worked out that way, and Tuesday’s overtime loss dropped the Hornets to 4-10. Making matters worse for Reid was an inadvertent elbow from Collin Sexton that he took to the nose late in overtime. He was subbed out and did not return. With Coby White and Brandon Miller shut down at the end of regulation, the Hornets lacked the options needed to potentially force a second overtime.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Coby White finished Tuesday’s loss to the Lakers with 19 points (6-of-12 FGs, 5-of-7 FTs), three rebounds, four assists, three steals and two three-pointers.
body: Although White has played in each of Charlotte’s last seven games, the team continues to limit his minutes. He logged 26 minutes on Tuesday and, along with Brandon Miller, did not play at all in overtime. The injuries and minutes restrictions the Hornets have dealt with have a lot to do with them being the worst fourth-quarter team in the NBA this season. Down the stretch on Tuesday, White and the other Hornets failed to do much offensively, with even inbounding the ball becoming an adventure. Charlotte doesn’t play again until Friday, which may be a good thing for White.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Kevon Looney finished Tuesday’s loss to the Hornets with four points (2-of-3 FGs) and seven rebounds.
body: With Walker Kessler (leg) out, the Lakers turned to Looney to start at center on Tuesday. While the veteran center grabbed seven rebounds, he played only 17 minutes, and his mobility was an issue. With Sandro Mamukelashvili (3/3/2/1) shooting 1-of-8 from the field, Lakers head coach JJ Redick eventually turned to two-way contract player Carson Cooper. While his numbers (3/4/2 in 18 minutes) won’t jump off the page, Cooper’s contributions as a rebounder and defender were one reason why the Lakers were able to rally. Kessler is expected to be available for Wednesday’s game against the Jazz, so Looney may find himself out of the rotation once again.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Luka Dončić tallied 36 points (13-of-34 FGs, 5-of-7 FTs), six rebounds, seven assists, one steal, one block and five three-pointers in Tuesday’s win over the Hornets.
body: Dončić didn’t have a great night shooting-wise, going 5-of-16 from three, but he still posted a complete stat line. The Lakers’ star has scored at least 32 points in 11 straight appearances, with the Lakers going 9-2 in those games. With Tuesday’s overtime win, the Lakers boast the best record in the Western Conference, something few expected at any point this season. Dončić has played like an MVP so far, whether the conversation is focused on the “actual” basketball or the fantasy basketball.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Quentin Grimes amassed 47 points (16-of-24 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), six rebounds, three assists, one steal and 10 three-pointers in Tuesday’s win over the Hornets.
body: Grimes had the best game of his career on Tuesday, and the Lakers needed it, trailing by as much as 18 late in the third quarter before rallying to win in overtime. Grimes scored 21 points in the fourth quarter alone, outscoring the Hornets by four, and his three-pointer with 1.7 seconds left forced overtime. Austin Reaves (heel) is supposed to test his injured heel on Wednesday before that night’s game against the Jazz, so we should learn more about how much time he’ll miss. Grimes, the first Laker other than Reaves, Luka Dončić or LeBron James to record a 30-point game since Dalton Knecht did in March 2025, will start as long as Reaves is out, and he’s worth rostering until that changes.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Darius Garland accumulated 20 points (5-of-15 FGs, 8-of-8 FTs), three rebounds, seven assists, one steal, one block and two three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Jazz.
body: While Garland kept the turnovers in check, committing one, and recorded a full stat line, he had a tough night shooting the basketball. The Clippers guard was 5-of-15 from the field, a far cry from his 50.6 percent shooting for the season. The biggest concern for him in fantasy basketball has been the turnovers, so there’s no need to lose sleep over Garland having an off shooting night.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Rui Hachimura amassed 20 points (7-of-10 FGs, 2-of-4 FTs), five rebounds, one assist, one steal, one block and four three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Jazz.
body: After scoring 24 points on 7-of-24 shooting in his previous three games, Hachimura needed a night like Tuesday, even if the Clippers were on the wrong end of a blowout. This was Hachimura’s second game this season with at least 20 points, five rebounds and five assists. Even better for fantasy managers was his 70 percent shooting from the field, a strong output for a player shooting 41.5 percent on the season.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Brook Lopez accounted for 23 points (8-of-16 FGs, 3-of-3 FTs), six rebounds, two assists, one steal, one block and four three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Jazz.
body: Lopez has scored at least 20 points in four of the Clippers’ last six games. The veteran center replaced Isaiah Jackson (eight points, five rebounds and two blocks) in the starting lineup just over two weeks ago and hasn’t looked back. Rostered in 44 percent of Yahoo leagues, Lopez deserves a little more attention in 12-team formats.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Mo Bamba finished Tuesday’s win over the Clippers with 15 points (6-of-7 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), 10 rebounds, three assists, one block and one three-pointer.
body: One game removed from going a perfect 6-of-6 from beyond the arc, Bamba recorded his first double-double of the season on Tuesday. While his season-long fantasy remains relatively low, Bamba has been close to a top-100 player over the past two weeks. Rostered in 34 percent of Yahoo leagues, he’s worth rostering because Utah is so shorthanded in the frontcourt.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Jrue Holiday accounted for 23 points (7-of-19 FGs, 4-of-6 FTs), five rebounds, six assists, two steals, one block and five three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Timberwolves.
body: With Deni Avdija ruled out, the Trail Blazers needed someone to step up offensively. Holiday was still used in a reserve role, but his 19 shot attempts tied him with Damian Lillard for the most on the team. Jrue finished with a full line, and he’s become a bit more valuable to fantasy managers since Ja Morant strained his hamstring. Jayson Kent started for Avdija, finishing with eight points, three rebounds, two steals and two three-pointers.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Donovan Clingan tallied 12 points (6-of-14 FGs, 0-of-3 FTs), 12 rebounds, four assists, one steal and one block in Tuesday’s loss to the Timberwolves.
body: Clingan wasn’t dominant against the Timberwolves, but he still thoroughly outplayed Rudy Gobert. The Trail Blazers’ center finished with his third straight double-double, and he’s recorded double-digit rebounds in five straight games. Add in the assists, and Clingan’s stat line may help compensate for the percentages.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Damian Lillard finished Tuesday’s loss to the Timberwolves with 25 points (8-of-19 FGs, 4-of-5 FTs), three rebounds, five assists, one steal and five three-pointers.
body: Lillard finished with 25 points, but his layup attempt in the final seconds, which would have given Portland the win, was blocked by Minnesota’s Trey Lyles. He’s scored at least 20 points in seven of the 10 games Portland has played since losing Ja Morant to a hamstring injury, providing top-100 fantasy value. Portland visits Milwaukee on Thursday in Lillard’s first game against the Bucks since being waived in the summer of 2025.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: LaMelo Ball recorded 18 points (7-of-17 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), nine rebounds, two assists, one steal and three three-pointers in Tuesday’s win over the Trail Blazers.
body: After recording at least five assists in five straight games, Ball had two in the Timberwolves’ two games against Portland. The good news for the Timberwolves was that they won both games, but that low assist number was a surprise. Ball finished Tuesday’s win one rebound shy of a double-double, offering unexpected value in that category. Even with the recent low assist numbers, field-goal percentage and turnovers remain Ball’s biggest issues in category leagues.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Jaden McDaniels amassed 22 points (10-of-16 FGs), five rebounds, four assists, three steals, one block and two three-pointers in Tuesday’s win over the Trail Blazers.
body: While McDaniels’ offensive production has been consistent throughout the season, fantasy managers may have hoped for a bit more from him in the aftermath of Anthony Edwards’ knee injury. He’s scored 20+ points three times since Edwards was injured in an October 26 loss to the Cavaliers, and his 23 points against the Trail Blazers matched his season high. That said, even with the scoring, McDaniels is still providing top-50 value in category leagues.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Ayo Dosunmu accounted for 30 points (11-of-19 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), four rebounds, five assists, one steal and seven three-pointers in Tuesday’s win over the Trail Blazers.
body: After scoring eight points on 3-of-11 shooting in Monday’s win over the Trail Blazers, Dosunmu rebounded in a big way in Tuesday’s rematch. Making his 10th straight start for the injured Anthony Edwards, Ayo recorded his first 30-point stat line of the season while shooting a high percentage from the field. Add in the rebounds, assists and three-pointers, and this was an excellent night for those rostering Dosunmu.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Luka Dončić, Quentin Grimes, Matisse Thybulle, Jake LaRavia and Kevon Looney will start Tuesday’s game against the Hornets.
body: Already playing without Austin Reaves, the Lakers won’t have Walker Kessler for Tuesday’s game. Looney moves into the starting lineup, and while he can provide rebounds in that role, Sandro Mamukelashvili is the superior fantasy option despite coming off the bench.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Coby White, Brandon Miller, Grant Williams, Naz Reid and Moussa Diabaté will start Tuesday’s game against the Lakers.
body: Hornets head coach Charles Lee has changed his starting lineup, with Williams replacing Sion James. Williams played 20 minutes in Sunday’s loss to the Clippers, hitting three three-pointers and scoring 11 points. While a solid defender, James is limited as a scorer, which may have factored into the lineup change.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Stephon Castle recorded 10 points (3-of-11 FGs, 2-of-4 FTs), two rebounds, seven assists and two three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Pistons.
body: Castle didn’t have a good night shooting the basketball, but he did provide solid value in the assists column. He has recorded six or more assists in three of his last four games and is averaging 5.5 assists per game for the season. De’Aaron Fox (6/2/2/2) also struggled against the Pistons, shooting 3-of-10 from the field, offering even less value to fantasy managers than Castle.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Devin Vassell finished Tuesday’s loss to the Pistons with 12 points (4-of-10 FGs, 2-of-3 FTs), five rebounds, four assists, one steal and two three-pointers.
body: A 2-of-4 night from beyond the arc isn’t much, but it was a step in the right direction for Vassell, who was 0-of-6 in wins over the Warriors and Jazz. A career 37.0 percent shooter from three, Devin entered Tuesday making a career-low 31.4 percent of his attempts. Fantasy managers rostering Vassell received solid value in rebounds and assists on Tuesday, but consistent three-point shooting is key for him.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Cade Cunningham, Daniss Jenkins, Kevin Huerter, Ausar Thompson and John Collins will start Tuesday’s game against the Spurs.
body: The Pistons won’t have Duncan Robinson, who is out for at least one week with a strained quad. Huerter moves into the starting lineup and is worth streaming, especially for fantasy managers needing three-point production.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Damian Lillard, Sidy Cissoko, Toumani Camara, Jayson Kent and Donovan Clingan will start Tuesday’s game against the Timberwolves.
body: Deni Avdija (foot) is out for Tuesday’s game, which frees up a spot in the Trail Blazers’ starting lineup. In his 10th appearance over two NBA seasons, Kent will make his first career start. He isn’t worth the risk as a streamer.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: LaMelo Ball, Ayo Dosunmu, Jaden McDaniels, Cody Williams and Rudy Gobert will start Tuesday’s game against the Trail Blazers.
body: Jonathan Kuminga (shoulder) is out for Tuesday’s game, opening up a spot in the Timberwolves’ starting lineup. Williams will fill the void, but the former lottery pick offers limited streaming value.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: De’Andre Hunter (hip) is questionable for Wednesday’s game against the Suns.
body: A late addition to the Kings’ injury report, Hunter did not play in Sunday’s loss to the Thunder. Dylan Cardwell replaced him in the starting lineup, with Keegan Murray moving to small forward. Expect the same on Wednesday if Hunter can’t play.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Deni Avdija (foot) is out for Tuesday’s game against the Timberwolves.
body: Due to left foot inflammation, Avdija will miss the second game of Portland’s back-to-back. Scoot Henderson is a potential replacement in the starting lineup, but he hasn’t done enough this season to merit streaming in most leagues.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Precious Achiuwa (ankle) is questionable for Wednesday’s game against the Suns.
body: Achiuwa did not play in Sunday’s loss to the Thunder, which factored into rookie Alex Karaban playing 29 minutes off the bench. Karaban didn’t score, and regardless of what happens with Achiuwa, he should only be rostered in dynasty leagues.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Zach LaVine (illness) is off the injury report for Wednesday’s game against the Suns.
body: A late scratch for Sunday’s loss to the Thunder, LaVine will be available on Wednesday. His return will push Malik Monk to the bench.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Thomas Sorber (knee) underwent a procedure on his right knee on Tuesday and will be re-evaluated in 6-8 weeks.
body: Sorber, who suffered a torn ACL during his lone season at Georgetown, missed the entire 2025-26 season and has yet to make his NBA debut. Late in his return-to-play process, the Thunder center developed inflammation in the patellofemoral joint of his right knee, necessitating Tuesday’s procedure. Sorber is expected to resume on-court activities in 6-8 weeks, but this does not affect fantasy basketball.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Neemias Queta (rest) is available for Wednesday’s game against the Nuggets.
body: Queta is back after sitting out Monday’s loss to the Magic, which was Boston’s second game in as many nights. His return likely pushes Luka Garza, who made a spot start and played 18 minutes against Orlando, to the bench.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: The Grizzlies announced on Tuesday that GG Jackson (foot) will be re-evaluated in three months.
body: Jackson suffered a broken fifth metatarsal in his right foot during Saturday’s win over the Nets. Tuesday’s surgical procedure was successful, and he’ll be re-evaluated in three months. Jerami Grant and Taylor Hendricks, who played 23 and 18 minutes, respectively, in Monday’s win over the Wizards, should absorb the minutes that would have gone to Jackson.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Jaylin Williams (back) is questionable for Wednesday’s game against the Hawks.
body: Williams has missed Oklahoma City’s last seven games, leaving the Thunder to count mainly on Isaiah Hartenstein and Aday Mara in the post. Mara’s minutes could decrease if JayWill returns, but he should still be in the rotation.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Jock Landale (hip) is out for Wednesday’s game against the Thunder.
body: Landale’s continued absence means that Zuby Ejiofor should remain in the rotation, although he logged just 12 minutes in Sunday’s win over the Bucks.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Kingston Flemings (back) is out for Wednesday’s game against the Thunder.
body: Flemings will miss a second straight game with a back injury. With CJ McCollum (calf) out for at least four weeks, the Hawks will have to rely more on Nickeil Alexander-Walker, Jalen Johnson and even Dyson Daniels as on-ball playmakers. As for the empty spot in the starting lineup, Luguentz Dort and Aaron Wiggins are two potential replacements.
author: Raphielle Johnson

headline: Scottie Barnes (illness) is available for Tuesday’s game against the Knicks.
body: Added to the Raptors’ injury report early Tuesday afternoon, Barnes will play despite being under the weather. Fantasy managers should make sure the star forward is in their active lineups before tip-off.
author: Raphielle Johnson
